title: One menu for a whole homelab

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You get a fresh server, and the list of things to install is long. What if you could just pick them from a menu?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's another-install-script. It's an interactive shell installer that sets up system configuration and deploys Docker containers from a text menu.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So it's a menu on top of a pile of install commands?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, and the neat part is the structure. Antoine kept the menu apart from the service definitions, so adding a new service doesn't mean stuffing more commands into the main setup script.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That keeps the entry point readable. Is it all shell?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Almost all of it. It's a shell project with a few Docker pieces and a little Python on the side, under the GPL license.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the takeaway is a homelab you can rebuild by choosing from a list instead of remembering commands.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. The full write-up on the page shows the components and the instructions.
